text: Great game and definitely worth the price, I would recommend buying while its on sale if you have the chance. The fighting is very fluid and only becomes more so when you get a better handle on the mechanics (parry, block, timing, combos). There are 4 different fighters with distinct styles and different sword types to augment the style of each fighter, so fighting can vary quite a bit from player to player. This game gets more and more fun as you learn to fight effectively, with matches becoming very entertaining to play or even watch in spectator mode. I'm looking forward to any add-on's that are in the future for this game.

title: blade symphony
text: This is an excellent game for hardcore skill junkies. It takes concentration, technique, strategie, precision, and calm thinking. Other than the fact that it requires more skill than just about every other game ever, it acts just like a brawler game. Customize you character, jump around the arena (I forgot to mention you can run on walls), and reduce your opponent to 0 HP. Each of the 4 playable characters have their own strengths and weaknesses. Judgement hits like a truck, but is very slow and easy to dodge. Phalanx hits hard and fast, but most of his attacks take hella accuracy. Pure and Ryoku are similar in the sense they both use kicks and flips in their basic attacks. Ryoku's attacks are very short range, making it easy for a decent Phalanx or Judgement to pick him off. Pure so far I've noticed has no downsides. Huge range, impossible to hit, lots of DPS. OP need nerf. Other than the fact that she's too strong, the game is well balanced, beautifully rendered, and very smooth to play. Absolutely worth the 15$.

text: For the most part, I have trouble giving this game a thumbs up since I know after this weekend I probably won't be playing with people who started the time I did. Although that only being the case, I can't really see why not to pick it up. With it soon being 75% off and now maybe one having a taste of the game, this might spike up the players. The combat is very well classed right now of all the people you can choose from. Sure, sometimes spamming is the way to go and can be frustrating to deal with, but the game offers helpful strategies to bypass this. Then after a person learns to mix and match their fighting moves, they then learn which one they like the best. With an interesting plot, good balancing that's simple, and nice play time to boot if there are players to play with, then this game is a must have for a fighter enthusiest.

text: What it plays like: Team Fortress meets HD minecraft. The good: - Plays smooth. - Every game plays differently and the classes add a lot of variety. - Lots of tactics, def & attack just about any way you can think of. - Leavers get replaced by other players. The bad: - Low elo matchmaking is plagued by a constant stream of leavers & AFK's and there is only a very minor penalty to it. Don't be surprised to have over 10 leavers in a match that lasts only 15 minutes. - High elo matchmaking is horrible. 10-25min wait-queue. - Game is often decided by matchmaking (some teammates are pure trolls or afk while the enemy team may have some decent ones). There's nothing you can do. - Game is no longer being developped (more or less abandoned). There are still nasty bugs & exploits like 6 vs 4 matches: I recommend to try this game for free as it can be fun for a few dozen hours, maybe a bit more. But after that you start running into it's flaws. I do not recommend putting any money into the game. There is no mixed option so I upvote it since it's free and still fun (for a short while).

text: The only competitive multiplayer-only FPS/MOBA that I actually enjoy is Block 'n Load. With all the comedy and style of TF2 on crack, maps and weapons of CS:GO on mushrooms, P2W elements of LoL on weed, characters of DOTA on meth, and gameplay like Ace of Spades on Adderall, Block 'n Load has all the great parts of games of the genres but better. Combine all of that with a community straight out of Insurgency, and a game methodology that rewards creativity and intelligence in equal parts as fast reflexes and good aim, and you have the best competitive game AS WELL AS FREE GAME I've played in a while (if not ever). If you have any questions, it's about those P2W elements I mentioned, since the trailers represent the game quite well. The way it works is this: perks (which rebalance your character in certain ways (like you get the team more building materials for every kill but get less for yourself) and new characters can both be bought with in-game currency, one which can be earned and one which can be bought with real money. The perks are dirt-cheap, however, and there are only enough characters that every week there is a 1/5 chance that one you want is on free rotation, with most of the "best" characters being fairly inexpensive. It took me less than ten hours of general play to "own" my first character, and it wasn't even one of the cheapest ones. The paid currency also gets you character skins, which are literally useless except to tell everybody who in the game has a bad sense of money management. One last warning for the wise: just because your team is being the "oh haha let's all be one character"♥♥♥♥♥♥for-brains group doesn't mean that the other team isn't too. You can't see eachothers teams until you start to load into the game proper, so once I jokingly said to my friend to look back at the team (from the loading screen) and his eye wasn't drawn to the fact that we had three of one character, but that the OTHER team had FIVE (the size of a whole team) of another character. We laughed a lot, and lost brutally.
